info.name: Bagisto Admin API
info.description:
Administrative endpoints for the [Bagisto](https://bagisto.com) e-commerce platform — catalog, sales, customers, marketing, settings, CMS and reporting. Both transports are covered: `REST/` and `GraphQL/`.

The full authentication guide, with sequence diagrams, curl and GraphQL examples and client notes, is [docs/authentication.md](https://github.com/bagisto/bagisto-api/blob/main/docs/authentication.md).

## Setup

1. Select the **Bagisto** environment (top right). Import it first if it is not in your workspace. One environment serves both the admin and the storefront collection.
2. Choose how to authenticate.

**As an app (login and refresh).** Set `adminEmail` and `adminPassword`, then run **REST → Auth → Log in with email and password**. It saves `adminAccessToken`, `adminRefreshToken` and `adminAccessTokenExpiresAt` to the environment. The access token lasts 15 minutes by default; before each request the collection renews it through `POST /api/admin/auth/refresh` when it expires within 60 seconds, so you only log in again once the refresh token or the session ends.

**With two-factor authentication.** When the admin has it enabled, the login answers `202` with `twoFactorRequired: true` and a `challengeToken` instead of tokens. The login request stores the challenge token in the collection variable `adminChallengeToken`; put the 6-digit code (or a `backup_code` instead of `code`) into the **Auth** two-factor request and send it within 5 minutes. It saves the tokens the same way.

**As a server integration (API token).** Create an API token under **Settings → API Tokens** in the admin panel (or with `php artisan bagisto-api:api-token:create`), bound to the domain the integration calls from, and paste it into `adminApiToken`. While `adminApiToken` is set it is sent on every request and nothing is refreshed. An API token is shown once, so copy it immediately.

| Variable | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `url` | Your store, e.g. `http://localhost:8000` |
| `adminEmail` / `adminPassword` | Any active admin user |
| `adminAccessToken` / `adminRefreshToken` / `adminAccessTokenExpiresAt` | Written by the login, two-factor and refresh requests |
| `adminApiToken` | An API token from **Settings → API Tokens**; leave it empty to use the login session |
| `adminChallengeToken` (collection variable) | Written by a login that needs a second factor |

The token is sent as the bearer on every request:

```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6Ii4uLiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
```

## The login flow

1. **Auth → Log in** returns the access token, the refresh token, the session, the admin and the role's `permissions`.
2. Every request sends the access token. When it expires, a request answers `401` with `error: access_token_expired`.
3. **Auth → Refresh** exchanges the refresh token for a **new pair**. The old refresh token stops working, and presenting it again is treated as theft: the whole session is revoked and every later refresh answers `refresh_token_invalid`. Run one refresh at a time.
4. On `401 refresh_token_invalid` (expired, used or revoked, or the session reached its absolute lifetime, 90 days by default), log in again.
5. **Auth → Log out** ends the session, **Log out of every session** ends all of the admin's sessions, and the sessions requests list and revoke them one by one. These, and **Update my account**, need a login session's access token; an API token gets `403 access_token_required`.

The lifetimes, rate limits and revocation rules are set in the admin panel under **Configuration → API → Admin Authentication**.

## Permissions

A token has exactly the permissions of the admin user's role, read on every request, so a valid token can still return **403** on an endpoint that user cannot reach. Login sessions are listed and revoked under **Auth** and **Settings → API Sessions**, and API tokens under **Settings → API Tokens**. API tokens are created in the admin panel or the console only.

## Errors worth handling

REST bodies carry the code in `error`; GraphQL errors carry it in `extensions.code`.

| Status and code | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `401 access_token_expired` | Refresh, then retry the request |
| `401 refresh_token_invalid` | Log in again |
| `401 unauthenticated` | The token is invalid, its session was revoked or the admin is inactive: log in again |
| `401 invalid_credentials` | Wrong email or password |
| `401 invalid_two_factor_code` / `two_factor_challenge_invalid` | Retry the code / log in again |
| `401 api_token_expired` / `api_token_revoked` | Create a new API token |
| `403 api_token_domain_mismatch` | Call from the domain the API token is bound to |
| `403 access_token_required` | Use a login session's access token, not an API token |
| `403 account_inactive` | An administrator must activate the admin |
| `429 too_many_login_attempts` / `too_many_password_requests` / `rate_limit_exceeded` | Wait for the `Retry-After` seconds |

## Layout

`REST/` and `GraphQL/` share one folder tree that mirrors the admin sidebar — `Settings/Currencies` holds exactly the endpoints behind that screen. `Auth` lists its requests in the order a client uses them. GraphQL is split into `Queries/` and `Mutations/` under each area.

## Worth knowing

- GraphQL requests declare only the arguments an operation **requires**, plus `first` where it paginates. The complete argument list for any operation is in the GraphiQL playground at `/api/admin/graphiql`.
- Postman's **Auto Fetch** runs a schema introspection query, which costs far more than a normal request. If things feel slow, switch it off and fetch the schema when you need it.

Full reference: [api-docs.bagisto.com](https://api-docs.bagisto.com/)

item.name: REST
item.description: Every REST endpoint, foldered by the API tag it belongs to.

request.description: Copies a section and its content into the same theme and channel. The copy is created switched off. Read the copy back with the section endpoint. Needs the `appearance.sections.create` permission; a footer links section cannot be copied (422), as a channel holds only one.

query.description: Channel ID (defaults to the current channel)

request.description: Creates a section against the theme and channel the request is scoped to. It is created switched off with a pending status draft, exactly as the appearance editor does, so an empty section is never put in front of shoppers before it is built.
Deletes the section and its content straight away, without staging; the storefront stops drawing it at once. Needs the `appearance.sections.delete` permission.

query.description: Channel ID (defaults to the current channel)

request.description: Throws away every staged draft (content, status and order) of the theme's sections on one channel, and returns the IDs of the sections that had one. An unknown theme is a 404.

One section by ID with its published values, any staged draft (`draftStatus`, `draftSortOrder` and each translation's `draftOptions`) and the content of every locale. Needs the `appearance.sections` permission; an unknown ID is a 404.

item.name: Get the editable fields of a section

query.description: Locale the options are read in

request.description: Returns the schema for the section's type and the options it currently holds — staged edits when there are any, otherwise the published values.

item.name: List the sections of a theme

query.description: Channel ID (defaults to the current channel)
Locale code the options are read in

request.description: Sections of the given theme for one channel, in render order with footer links pinned last. Scope with `?channel=` and `?locale=`; both fall back the way the appearance editor does.

item.name: Preview a theme with staged edits applied

query.description: Channel ID (defaults to the current channel)
Locale the options are read in

request.description: The sections a channel would draw if the staged edits were published: draft options replace published ones, draft status and order are applied, sections switched off are left out, and footer links stay last.

query.description: Channel ID (defaults to the current channel)

request.description: Makes every staged draft (content, status and order) of the theme's sections on one channel live on the storefront, and returns the IDs of the sections published. An unknown theme is a 404.

Stages a new render order for every section of one theme and channel. Nothing changes on the storefront until POST /appearance/themes/{code}/sections/publish; a partial, mixed-scope or unknown list of section IDs is refused with 422.

Stages switching one section on or off as a draft (`status` is required). The storefront keeps the published status until the theme's staged edits are published; the answer says whether the section still has a draft.
Holds the options as an unpublished draft for the locale. The storefront keeps drawing the published values until the theme is published.
Writes the published values of a section. Send `options` with `?locale=` to write that locale's published content; use the draft endpoint to stage edits instead.
Stores one image or video against the section and returns the path to record in its options. Send `multipart/form-data` with a `file` field. Needs the `appearance.sections.edit` permission.

formdata.description: An image (bmp, jpeg, jpg, png, webp) or a video (mp4, webm, ogg) of at most 50 MB.

request.description: Points the given channels at the theme. Sections belonging to a channel's previous theme are left in place but stop being drawn — call the impact endpoint first to see what that affects.

One theme from the gallery by its code, installed or not, with whether it is installed, its status and the channels it is active on. Needs the `appearance.themes` permission; an unknown code is a 404.
Every theme this installation knows about — installed ones and the ones available to install — with the channels each is active on. Active themes come first.

item.name: Report what activating a theme would leave behind

query.description: Channel IDs the theme would be applied to

request.description: Lists the channels that already hold sections built for their current theme, with how many. A channel whose sections would survive is not listed.

item.name: Log in with email and password

request.description: Starts a session and returns a short-lived JWT access token and a refresh token. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` and exchange the refresh token at `/api/admin/auth/refresh` before or after the access token expires. When the admin has two-factor authentication enabled, the response is `202` with `twoFactorRequired: true` and a single-use `challengeToken` valid for 5 minutes by default, and no tokens: send it with the code to `/api/admin/auth/two-factor`. Five failed attempts per email and address lock the login for 60 seconds by default; both are configurable under Configuration → API → Admin Authentication → Login Protection.

exec: console.info('A second factor is required: send the code with the Auth two-factor request (POST /auth/two-factor).');

item.name: Finish a login with a two-factor code

request.description: Exchanges the `challengeToken` of a `202` login, with the 6-digit authenticator `code` or a `backupCode`, for the access and refresh token pair. A challenge works once and for 5 minutes by default; five wrong codes revoke it, and five wrong codes a minute for the same admin (configurable) lock further codes for that minute. A code from an already used time window is refused, and a backup code is used up.

exec: console.info('A second factor is required: send the code with the Auth two-factor request (POST /auth/two-factor).');

item.name: Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair

request.description: Returns a new access token and a new refresh token in the same session; the refresh token sent stops working. Presenting a refresh token that was already used revokes the whole session. Once the refresh token expires, or the session reaches its absolute lifetime, log in again.

exec: console.info('A second factor is required: send the code with the Auth two-factor request (POST /auth/two-factor).');

request.description: Returns the profile of the currently authenticated admin, with the kind of token sent (`session` for a login access token, `api_token` for an API token), its session or API token id, and when it expires (null for an API token without expiry).

item.name: List the signed-in admin's active sessions

request.description: Every live login session of the calling admin, newest first, with where each was last used from. `isCurrent` marks the session of the access token sent. Needs a login session access token.
Revokes one live session of the calling admin, for example a lost phone; its access and refresh tokens stop working at once. Revoking the current session logs it out.

item.name: Log out of the current session

request.description: Revokes the session the access token belongs to, so its access and refresh tokens stop working at once. Needs a login session access token, not an API token.
Revokes every session of the signed-in admin, on every device, including the current one. Needs a login session access token, not an API token.

Sends core's admin password reset email when the address belongs to an admin. The answer is the same whether or not it does. Five requests a minute per client address are allowed by default (configurable).

item.name: Reset a password with the emailed token

request.description: Sets a new password with the token from the reset email, through core's admin password broker. Every API session of the admin is revoked, and every API token too when *Revoke API Tokens on Password Change* is on; log in again afterwards. Five requests a minute per client address are allowed by default (configurable).

Updates the signed-in admin's name, email and password, as the admin panel's *My Account* screen does; `currentPassword` is always required. Changing the password revokes the admin's other sessions (the current one stays signed in) when *Revoke Sessions on Password Change* is on, and every API token when *Revoke API Tokens on Password Change* is on. Needs a login session access token, not an API token.

item.name: CMS page detail with all translations + channels

request.description: One CMS page by ID, with the translation of every locale and the channels it is shown on. An unknown ID is a 404.

Mirrors Bagisto admin CMS → Pages → Create. Top-level translated fields (page_title, html_content, etc.) are broadcast to every locale by the PageRepository. Validates url_key (required + unique on cms_page_translations + slug regex), page_title, html_content, and channels (non-empty array of existing channel ids).

body.raw:
{ "url_key": "about-us", "page_title": "About Us", "html_content": "

About Us

Welcome.

", "channels": [ 1 ], "meta_title": "About Us", "meta_keywords": "about,us,company", "meta_description": "Learn more about our company." }

request.description: Deletes the CMS page, so its URL stops resolving on the storefront. An unknown ID is a 404.

item.name: Export CMS pages as csv, xls or xlsx

request.description: Downloads the CMS Pages datagrid as a csv, xls or xlsx file — the same data the admin CMS → Pages "view" listing shows (ID, Page Title, URL Key, Channel, Locale). Honours the same filters as the listing (`id`, `page_title`, `url_key`, `channel`, `locale`). The response is a binary download, not JSON.
Paginated, filterable, sortable CMS pages list mirroring the admin CMS → Pages datagrid.
Deletes a batch of CMS pages. Non-existent IDs are silently skipped (mirrors monolith).

Mirrors Bagisto admin CMS → Pages → Edit. Validation is LOCALE-NESTED: `<locale>.url_key`, `<locale>.page_title`, `<locale>.html_content` are required. Top-level: `channels` (required), `locale` (required — names which locale block is being updated). url_key uniqueness excludes the current page.

item.name: Attribute family detail with attribute groups and attributes

request.description: Returns one attribute family with all attribute groups and their associated attributes (including pivot position).
Creates an attribute family with optional nested attribute groups and per-group custom_attributes. `code` must be unique and pass the Code rule.
Refuses the default family (HTTP 400), which backs every product form, and any family a product is using (HTTP 400).

query.description: Filter by family ID — single integer or comma-separated list.

request.description: Paginated, filterable, sortable attribute family list mirroring the admin Catalog → Families datagrid.
Updates an attribute family. Inside `attribute_groups`, items keyed by numeric id update existing groups; items keyed by `group_*` create new groups; omitted existing ids are deleted.

item.name: Add an option to a select/multiselect/checkbox attribute

request.description: Creates a new option for the given attribute. Only allowed when the attribute type is `select`, `multiselect`, or `checkbox`.

item.name: Attribute detail with translations and options

request.description: Returns one attribute with all locale translations and all options (each option also includes its own translations). For `select`, `multiselect`, and `checkbox` types, the `options` array is fully populated; for all other types it is `null`.

Creates an attribute with optional translations and options (for select/multiselect/checkbox types). The `code` must be unique, pass the Code rule (letters/digits/underscore), and not be a reserved word (`type`, `attribute_family_id`).
Deletes a user-defined attribute. Returns HTTP 403 for system attributes, HTTP 409 if the attribute is used in attribute families.
Deletes the given option. Returns HTTP 409 if the option is referenced by any product attribute values.

query.description: Filter by attribute ID — single integer or comma-separated list (e.g. "1" or "1,2").

request.description: Paginated, filterable, sortable attribute list mirroring the admin Catalog → Attributes datagrid.

Deletes a batch of user-defined attributes. If any ID in the batch belongs to a system attribute (`is_user_defined = 0`), the entire batch is rejected with HTTP 422. Non-existent IDs are silently skipped.
Updates an attribute. The `code` field cannot be changed (returns 422 if a different code is supplied). Changing `type` is refused when product attribute values exist.
Partially updates the given option. Only supplied fields are changed; translations merge per-locale.
Returns one category with the full translations array and the list of filterable attribute IDs.

query.description: Filter by status (0 = disabled, 1 = enabled). Nodes with no qualifying descendants are pruned.
Limit tree to descendants of this category ID (inclusive). Returns empty array if the ID is unknown.

request.description: Full nested category tree. Supports optional locale, status, and rootId filters. Returns a JSON array of root nodes.

Mirrors Bagisto admin Catalog → Categories → Create. Validates slug (unique), name, position, attributes. `description` required when `display_mode` is `description_only` or `products_and_description`. File-upload for `logo_path` / `banner_path` is NOT supported in v1.
Refuses with HTTP 400 if the category is the root (id=1) or referenced as `channels.root_category_id`.

query.description: Filter by category ID — single integer or comma-separated list (e.g. "12" or "12,18").

request.description: Paginated, filterable, sortable category list mirroring the admin Catalog → Categories datagrid.
Deletes a batch of categories. If any ID is non-deletable (root or a channel root_category_id), the entire batch is rejected with HTTP 400. Non-existent IDs are silently skipped.
Sets the status of a batch of categories to the given value (0 or 1).

Mirrors Bagisto admin Catalog → Categories → Edit. Validation is LOCALE-NESTED: `<locale>.slug`, `<locale>.name`, `<locale>.description` (when display_mode requires it) are required. Top-level fields: `position`, `attributes`, `parent_id`, `display_mode`, `status`. Moving a category is done via this endpoint with `parent_id` + `position` (no separate /move endpoint — parity with Bagisto admin which has no move action).

item.name: Add a customer-group price to a product

request.description: Creates a new tier-price row. `customer_group_id: null` makes the price apply to every customer group. The combination `(qty, customer_group_id)` must be unique per product.

item.name: Bulk-update a product's per-source inventory quantities

request.description: Mirrors Bagisto monolith ProductController::updateInventories. Fires catalog.product.update.before / catalog.product.update.after. Returns the updated listing payload — same shape as GET.

Returns a single catalog product with all detail-level fields populated. `channels` lists every available channel, each flagged `assigned` for this product. `attributes` mirrors the admin edit screen field-for-field — every attribute the product's family defines (code, adminName, type, value, options, per-channel/locale flags), with empty fields present (value null). Type-specific blocks (superAttributes/variants, bundleOptions, linkedProducts, downloadableLinks/downloadableSamples) are populated only for the matching product type; all others are null.

variable.description: ID of the product to copy

request.description: Duplicates an existing product across all attribute_values, images, inventories, categories and customer_group_prices. Refuses variants (parent_id != null) with HTTP 422. Mirrors Bagisto monolith ProductController::copy. Fires catalog.product.create.before and catalog.product.create.after.

item.name: Create a catalog product (step 1 — all 7 types)

request.description: Mirrors the Bagisto admin Create-Product wizard step 1: only sku + attribute_family_id + type are submitted (plus super_attributes when type=configurable). Name, description, price, inventories, etc. are added in the step-2 update endpoint (Phase 5.9). Accepts type ∈ {simple, virtual, downloadable, grouped, bundle, configurable, booking}. For type=configurable, super_attributes is required and must be a non-empty map of attribute code (or id) → option_ids — the core repository generates the full Cartesian-product of variants. For booking, the 5 sub-types (default/appointment/event/rental/table) are configured during step-2 update. Returns the full AdminCatalogProduct detail payload — most fields will be null because only sku/type/family are populated yet. Fires catalog.product.create.before and catalog.product.create.after.

Deletes a catalog product. For configurable products, all variants cascade. No "refuse if in non-completed order" guard (mirrors Bagisto admin behaviour). Fires catalog.product.delete.before / catalog.product.delete.after. Returns 204 on success.
Deletes one customer-group (tier) price row of the product. An unknown product, or a row that does not belong to it, is a 404.
Deletes the DB row and removes the file from public storage.
Deletes the DB row and removes the file from public storage.

variable.description: Attribute ID whose stored file path should be streamed.

request.description: Streams the stored file for the given product attribute (a downloadable product's file/sample attribute) as a binary attachment. Send `Accept: application/octet-stream`. Binary download, not JSON.

item.name: Export products as csv, xls or xlsx

query.description: Export format: csv, xls or xlsx. Defaults to csv.

request.description: Downloads the products datagrid as a csv, xls or xlsx file — the same data the admin Catalog → Products Export button produces. Honours the same filters as the listing and exports every matching row, not just the current page. Binary download, not JSON. Pick the file type with ?format=csv|xls|xlsx (default csv).

query.description: Filter by product ID — single integer or comma-separated list (e.g. "1,2,3").
Price range shorthand — "min,max" (e.g. "10,500"). Overridden by price_from / price_to when both are present.

request.description: Paginated, filterable, sortable product list mirroring the admin Catalog → Products datagrid. Routes via Elasticsearch when the admin panel is configured to. Returns a `{ data, meta }` envelope.

item.name: List customer-group (tier) prices for a product

request.description: Returns every customer-group price row attached to the product, wrapped in the standard admin `{ data, meta }` envelope.

item.name: List per-source inventory rows for a product

request.description: Returns one row per inventory_source that has a product_inventories entry for this product. The envelope meta carries totalQty — the sum across all sources.

Deletes a batch of products. Non-existent IDs are silently skipped. If any single delete throws an exception, the endpoint returns 500 with the underlying message — matching the Bagisto monolith ProductController::massDestroy behaviour.
Sets the status of a batch of products to the given value (0 or 1). Mirrors Bagisto monolith ProductController::massUpdate — best-effort, fires catalog.product.update.{before,after} per ID.
Updates the position of one or more existing images for the given product. Each image id must belong to the product; otherwise the call is rejected.

Partial update (PATCH-style): send only the fields you want to change — every attribute on the product's family is editable by its code (sku, name, url_key, short_description, description, meta_title, color, size, brand, price, weight, status, …). Translatable fields are written to the requested locale; pass `?locale=fr&channel=default` to target a specific locale/channel (defaults to the store default). Omitted fields keep their current value. Type-structure keys are accepted for the matching type: `variants` (configurable), `bundle_options` (bundle), `links` (grouped), `downloadable_links`/`downloadable_samples` (downloadable), `booking` (booking). `categories`/`channels`/`related_products`/`up_sells`/`cross_sells` replace the current set when sent (omit to keep). Sub-resources `images`/`videos`/`inventories`/`customer_group_prices` have dedicated endpoints and are ignored here (noted in `_warnings`). Returns the full product detail (same shape as GET /catalog/products/{id}).
Partially updates the given tier-price row. The new `(qty, customer_group_id)` combination must remain unique for the product.
Edits what is stored alongside an uploaded image — its alt text and its position. The file itself is replaced by uploading a new image and deleting this one.

Uploads the binary file for a file-type downloadable link and returns its stored path. Send as multipart/form-data with `file`. The returned `path` is what you then set on the link via the product update (`downloadable_links[link_x][file] = path`, `type = file`). URL-type links do not need this — set their `url` directly on update.

formdata.description: The link file, at most 128 MB. It is stored on the private disk.

request.description: Uploads the binary file for a file-type downloadable sample and returns its stored path. Send as multipart/form-data with `file`. The returned `path` is what you then set on the sample via the product update (`downloadable_samples[sample_x][file] = path`, `type = file`).

formdata.description: The sample file, at most 128 MB. It is stored on the private disk.

request.description: Uploads a new image for the given product. Send as multipart/form-data with `image` containing the file (allowed mime types: bmp, jpeg, jpg, png, webp). Optional `alt_text` is stored for every locale the request covers.
Uploads a new video for the given product. Send as multipart/form-data with `video` containing the file (mp4, webm, ogg). Optional `position`.

item.name: Bulk-update configuration values for one slug

request.description: Upserts every value in `values` under the given slug, validating server-side against each field's registered `validation` string. Send as `application/json` for scalars or as `multipart/form-data` (with `values[<dotted.code>]` as the file part) when uploading file/image fields.

query.description: When true, embeds the effective value per field.

request.description: Returns the merged system_config tree. Use `?slug=<section>.<group>` to scope to one node. `?include_values=true` embeds the effective value per field (uses `?channel=` and `?locale=` for resolution).
Lists every registered configuration slug (section/group key) with its label, so a client can discover the valid slugs to pass to the configuration values endpoint.

query.description: Channel code for resolution. Defaults to the requested channel.
Locale code for resolution. Defaults to the requested locale.

request.description: Returns the flat `key → string` map of effective values for every field under the given slug. Falls back to per-field defaults when no `core_config` row exists.
Deletes the GDPR request record only; no customer data is touched. An unknown ID is a 404.

item.name: Download a GDPR data export for a customer

request.description: Returns a JSON dump of every table referencing the customer's id (orders, addresses, reviews, wishlists, notes). No request body — the customer is identified by the path.
One customer GDPR request by ID: its type, status, message and the customer who made it. An unknown ID is a 404.
Paginated, filterable, sortable list. Returns the standard { data, meta } admin envelope.
Sets status to "approved" and, for type=delete requests, cascades the customer deletion. Refuses to re-process an already-approved request.
Update the request status. Allowed status values: pending, processing, declined, approved. Use the /process endpoint to also perform the destructive side-effect for delete requests.
New groups are always created with is_user_defined=1 (system groups cannot be created via API).
One customer group by ID, with whether it is user-defined and how many customers belong to it. An unknown ID is a 404.
Refuses if the group is a system group (is_user_defined=0) or has customers attached (400).
Paginated, filterable, sortable list. Returns the standard { data, meta } admin envelope.
System groups and groups with attached customers are skipped with a reason.
System groups refuse code/is_user_defined changes (422). Only name can be updated for system groups.

item.name: Add a product to the draft cart

request.description: Adds the product to the cart using the shared `Cart::addProduct` flow — supports every product type. Body keys mirror the storefront add-to-cart payload (`productId`, `quantity`, plus type-specific `selectedConfigurableOption`, `superAttribute`, `bundleOptions`, `links`, `qty[]`, etc).
Applies a coupon code to the draft cart. Returns 404 if the coupon is unknown / inactive; 422 if the same coupon is already applied; 200 on success.

item.name: Create an empty draft cart for a customer

request.description: Bootstraps an empty admin draft cart (`is_active = false`) for the given customer. The returned `cartId` is the handle the admin uses for the rest of the Create-Order flow (`POST /api/admin/carts/{id}/items`, addresses, shipping, payment, place-order).
Returns the admin draft cart with items, totals, addresses, and selected shipping / payment.

item.name: List available shipping rates for the draft cart

request.description: Calls `Shipping::collectRates()` against the cart and returns the available rates. Requires both billing AND shipping addresses to already be saved — returns HTTP 409 otherwise.

item.name: List supported payment methods for the draft cart

request.description: Returns `Payment::getSupportedPaymentMethods()`. A shipping method must already be selected on the cart (HTTP 409 otherwise).

item.name: Place an order from a draft cart

request.description: Finalises the given draft cart into an order. Mirrors the monolith `admin.sales.orders.store` flow. Returns 409 if a prerequisite (addresses / shipping / payment method) is missing, and 422 if the payment method is not in `['cashondelivery', 'moneytransfer']`.
Removes the cart item identified by `cartItemId` from the draft cart and recollects totals.
